problem: At the craft fair, Tomasz picked out 12 glass beads and his aunt picked out 9 wooden beads. How many beads did the two of them choose in all?
follow_up_questions: On the way home 8 beads rolled out of the bag and were lost. How many beads did they still have?
Back home, his aunt found 15 more beads in a drawer and added them. How many beads do they have now?

problem: How many shells did Priya and her grandmother collect on the beach if Priya found 12 and her grandmother found 9?
follow_up_questions: The waves washed 8 of the shells out of their bucket. How many shells were left in it?
Later her grandmother bought a bag of 15 shells at the beach shop and tipped them into the bucket. How many shells are in the bucket now?

problem: A pond had 52 ducks on it at dawn. By lunchtime, 47 of them had flown away. How many ducks stayed on the pond?
How many stamps were left in Ms. Ferreira's drawer? She started the week with 52 stamps and used 47 of them on party invitations.
At the swimming gala, 41 swimmers took part. 9 of them used goggles from the lost-property box and the others used their own. How many swimmers used their own goggles?
follow_up_questions: After the first race, 12 of the swimmers with their own goggles went to the changing rooms. How many of them were still by the pool?

problem: Out of 41 children on the museum trip, 9 had a ticket paid for by the school. The rest brought their own tickets. Find how many children brought their own.
follow_up_questions: At noon, 12 of the children with their own tickets left for the café. How many of those children were still in the galleries?

problem: Mira sells homemade cookies for 20 cents each. Before school ended she had sold 9 cookies. How much money did she make?
follow_up_questions: After school she sold 6 more cookies. How much did she make that day in total?
She spent 85 cents on a new ribbon for her stall. How much money is left?

problem: Kwame had sold 9 bookmarks by noon at the school fair, and each one cost 20 cents. What had he earned so far?
follow_up_questions: In the afternoon he sold another 6 bookmarks. What did he earn over the whole fair?
A roll of tape for the stall cost him 85 cents. How much does he have after paying for it?

problem: Paper plates for the class picnic are sold in stacks of 10. Mr. Ibrahim needs 70 plates. How many stacks should he buy?
follow_up_questions: He hands 2 of the stacks to the class next door. How many plates does he keep?

problem: A florist needs 70 roses for a wedding, and the roses arrive in bunches of 10. Work out how many bunches she must order.
follow_up_questions: She gives 2 bunches to her helper for the tables. How many roses are left for her own work?

problem: At the school bake sale, 90 dollars were collected. Some of the cakes had pink icing. Parents gave 30 dollars as donations, and the rest came from selling cakes. How much money came from the cakes?
What did the lemonade stand earn from selling drinks? On Sunday it took in 90 dollars, and 30 dollars of that was from a jar of donations. A breeze kept knocking over the sign.
Lena packed 50 crayons into her school bag on Friday. During art class, 20 of them fell out and were left behind. How many crayons did she bring home?
follow_up_questions: On Monday her teacher returned 10 of the missing crayons. How many crayons does Lena have now?
She sorts them into 5 equal boxes. How many crayons are in each box?
She gives 2 of the boxes to her brother. How many crayons does she keep?

problem: How many seashells did Mateo carry back from the beach? He had gathered 50 of them in a net bag, but 20 slipped through a hole on the walk to the car.
follow_up_questions: The next morning his cousin found 10 of the dropped shells and brought them over. How many shells does Mateo have now?
He spreads them evenly over 5 shelves. How many shells sit on each shelf?
He gives away the shells from 2 shelves. How many shells does he still have?

problem: At the school fair, Omar paid 40 cents for a balloon and 50 cents for a cup of juice. How much did he spend in total?
follow_up_questions: He came with 95 cents. How much money is left?
His friend Ruth bought only a cup of juice. How much less did Ruth spend than Omar?

problem: A pencil cost Ines 40 cents and an eraser cost her 50 cents at the station kiosk. Find how much she paid for the two things.
follow_up_questions: There were 95 cents in her pocket before. How much is in her pocket now?
Her brother bought just an eraser. How much less than Ines did he spend?

problem: A school group is hiking a 30-kilometre trail to a lake. By the first rest stop they have walked 18 kilometres. How many kilometres do they still have to walk?
follow_up_questions: They walk 6 kilometres each hour. How many hours until they reach the lake?
How many kilometres is the hike to the lake and back again?
Their club's logbook showed 35 kilometres before this hike. What will it show after they walk to the lake and back?

problem: How far is left for the boat? A ferry has a 30-mile crossing to an island, and it has already sailed 18 miles.
follow_up_questions: The ferry travels 6 miles every hour. In how many hours will it reach the island?
What is the total distance of the crossing there and back?
The ferry's trip counter read 35 miles before it left port. What will it read after it returns?

problem: A snail is trying to climb a garden wall that is 90 centimetres tall. By evening it had crawled only 30 centimetres up. How much farther does it have to go?
follow_up_questions: The next day it climbed twice as high as on the first day. How far below the top was it then?

problem: How many more steps must Arturo climb? The tower in the old castle has 90 steps, and he has stopped to rest after 30.
follow_up_questions: On his second visit he climbed twice as many steps before resting. How many steps from the top was he then?

problem: Dad is taking the twins skating on Saturday. He rents two pairs of skates at 4 dollars a pair and one locker for 6 dollars. How much does he pay?
follow_up_questions: He pays with a 20-dollar note. How much change does he get?
On Sunday he rents 3 more lockers for his friends. What do those cost?
How much did he spend at the rink on Saturday and Sunday together?

problem: How much will Mrs. Chen pay at the bookshop for two notebooks and one pen, if a notebook is 4 dollars and a pen is 6 dollars?
follow_up_questions: She hands over a 20-dollar bill. How much change comes back?
The next day she goes back for 3 more pens. What do they cost?
What did she spend at the bookshop on the two days together?

problem: Sven has 46 returned library books to stack on a trolley, 10 books to a stack. Once he has made all the full stacks he can, how many books are left over?
follow_up_questions: How many full stacks are on the trolley?

problem: Eggs from the farm go into trays of 10. Amara collected 46 eggs this morning. After filling as many trays as she can, how many eggs are left outside a tray?
follow_up_questions: How many trays did she fill?

problem: On Monday the librarian counted the pencils: 7 full boxes holding 10 pencils each, plus 4 loose ones in a drawer. How many pencils does the library have?
follow_up_questions: During the week, 50 pencils were handed out to pupils. How many were left?
On Friday the leftover pencils were shared equally among 6 classrooms. How many did each classroom get?
Each classroom put 3 in the teacher's desk and gave the rest to pupils. How many pencils went to pupils altogether?

problem: How many stickers does Leila have? She has 7 sheets of stickers with 10 on each sheet, plus 4 stickers loose in her pencil case.
follow_up_questions: She used 50 of them to decorate her scrapbook. How many stickers remain?
She gives all the remaining stickers to her 6 cousins, the same number to each. How many does each cousin get?
Each cousin sticks 3 on a birthday card and keeps the rest. How many stickers do the cousins keep altogether?

problem: Mum is baking for a class party where 9 children are coming. Each child gets one cupcake. How many cupcakes does she need?
follow_up_questions: Each cupcake is topped with 3 strawberries. How many strawberries are used?

problem: Every camper sleeps in one sleeping bag. How many sleeping bags must the leader pack for 9 campers?
follow_up_questions: Each sleeping bag is tied with 3 straps. How many straps are needed?

problem: In the school show, 13 dancers perform, each in a pair of ballet shoes. What is the total number of ballet shoes on stage?
follow_up_questions: The teacher also keeps 6 spare shoes backstage. How many shoes are there in all?
After the show, all the shoes are packed into boxes of 4. How many boxes are filled?

problem: How many gloves do 13 goalkeepers at the football camp wear, if each of them wears a pair?
follow_up_questions: The camp has 6 extra gloves in the kit bag too. What is the total number of gloves?
At the end of the day the gloves go into bags of 4. How many bags are filled?

problem: A school group of 48 pupils visits the zoo with 2 guides. Each guide leads the same number of pupils. How many pupils are in each guide's group?
follow_up_questions: One guide has already shown 15 of her pupils the lions. How many in her group have still not seen them?

problem: How many apples go into each basket when a farmer divides 48 apples evenly between 2 baskets?
follow_up_questions: From the first basket, 15 apples are sold. How many are still in that basket?

problem: At the end of the school year, 45 pencils were left in the art room. Mr. Duarte shared them equally among 5 pupils. How many pencils did each pupil get?
follow_up_questions: One pupil lost 4 of her pencils. How many pencils does she have left?
Then she buys 7 more at the stationery shop. How many pencils does she have now?
She snaps every one of them in half to make short pencils. How many halves does she get?

problem: Grandpa has 45 plums from his tree and gives the same number to each of his 5 grandchildren. What is each grandchild's share?
follow_up_questions: Ana eats 4 of her plums. How many does she have left?
Her mum gives her 7 more plums. How many does Ana have now?
She cuts each plum in half for a tart. How many halves are there?

problem: The art teacher puts 60 paintbrushes into 10 jars, the same number in every jar. She opens the windows for fresh air. How many paintbrushes stand in one jar?
How many seeds go into each pot if a gardener shares 60 seeds equally among 10 pots? Her cat sleeps on the warm windowsill.
The coach shares 32 cones equally among the 4 corners of the football pitch. How many cones go at each corner?
follow_up_questions: At the last corner, she adds 5 more cones. How many cones are at that corner now?

problem: How many photos fit on each page if Mia spreads 32 holiday photos equally over 4 album pages?
follow_up_questions: On the last page she glues 5 extra photos. How many photos are on the last page now?

problem: At the campsite, each field fits 4 tents. There are 28 tents to put up. How many fields are needed?
follow_up_questions: Each tent sleeps 2 campers. How many campers can sleep there at once?
If 49 campers arrive, how many sleeping spots will be empty?
Each camper who arrived pays 3 dollars for the night. How much money is collected?

problem: How many shelves does the toy library need, if it has 28 board games to put away and each shelf holds 4 games?
follow_up_questions: Each game is played by 2 children. How many children can play at the same time?
If 49 children come to games afternoon, how many places will be empty?
Each child who came pays 3 dollars for snacks. How much money is collected?

problem: A scout leader has a rope 36 feet long. Each tent needs 4 feet of rope to tie it down. How many tents can the scouts tie down?
follow_up_questions: Every tent also needs 2 pegs. How many pegs will the scouts need?

problem: How many bracelets can Jaya make from 36 beads if each bracelet uses 4 beads?
follow_up_questions: Each bracelet gets 2 tiny bells. How many bells does she need?

problem: A board game at the toy shop costs 37 dollars. Grandma pays with a 50 dollar note. The shop has a big rocking horse by the door. How much change does Grandma get?
What change does Ravi receive? He buys football boots priced at 37 dollars and hands over 50 dollars. The boots are bright orange.
At the stationery shop, Mr. Lindgren picks up two packs of pencils, 15 pencils per pack. How many pencils is that altogether?
follow_up_questions: He gives 8 of them to his class straight away. How many does he have left?

problem: There are 15 eggs in a carton, and Fatima puts two cartons in her basket at the market. How many eggs does she have?
follow_up_questions: She uses 8 eggs to bake a cake. How many eggs are left?

problem: Amir's teacher hands him 34 crayons and two empty boxes. He must put the same number of crayons in each box. How many crayons go in one box?
follow_up_questions: Amir then adds 3 markers to each box. How many things are in one box now?
What is the total number of things in both boxes?

problem: How many marbles go in each jar if Elena splits 34 marbles evenly between two jars?
follow_up_questions: She drops 3 shiny pebbles into each jar too. How many objects are in one jar now?
How many objects are in both jars together?

problem: The school librarian is sending 80 books to a village school. She packs 10 books in every crate. How many crates does she fill?
follow_up_questions: Each crate also gets 3 bookmarks. How many bookmarks are needed?
She already has 15 bookmarks in her drawer. How many more does she need to find?
If a teacher takes 2 of the crates to her classroom, how many crates are still in the library?

problem: How many baskets can the farm shop fill with 80 apples, putting 10 in each?
follow_up_questions: Each basket also gets 3 jars of jam. How many jars of jam are needed?
There are 15 jars of jam already on the shelf. How many more jars must the shop bring out?
A customer buys 2 of the baskets. How many baskets are left in the shop?

problem: Ms. Novak's dance class has 26 pupils, and they all dance in pairs. How many pairs are on the floor?
follow_up_questions: Each pair needs one hoop, but there are only 9 hoops. How many more hoops does she need?

problem: How many pairs of socks can Ben make from 26 single socks in the laundry basket?
follow_up_questions: He has only 9 clothes pegs, one for each pair. How many more pegs does he need to hang every pair?

problem: Every game at the arcade costs 3 tokens. Ollie has 21 tokens in his pocket. What is the number of games he can play?
follow_up_questions: His mum gives him 9 more tokens. How many tokens does he have now?
If each game still costs 3 tokens, how many games can he play now?

problem: How many stickers can Zara trade for at the school swap if she has 21 marbles and each sticker costs 3 marbles?
follow_up_questions: Her brother gives her 9 more marbles. How many marbles does she have now?
If each sticker still costs 3 marbles, how many stickers can she get now?

problem: In the kitchen shop, 10 matching stools have 30 legs in all. Maya's brother wants to know how many legs 7 of those stools have. What is the answer?
follow_up_questions: How many fewer legs is that than on all the stools in the shop?

problem: How many bananas are in 7 bunches, if Kofi counts 30 bananas on the 10 identical bunches at the fruit stall?
follow_up_questions: How many fewer bananas is that than on all the bunches at the stall?

problem: Six jars of jam fit in one box. Hira has 48 jars from her grandfather's farm to pack. How many boxes will she fill?
How many teams will there be if a coach divides 48 players into teams of six?
Stickers at the school shop cost 5 cents each. If Kofi spends his 65 cents only on stickers, how many can he buy?
follow_up_questions: He sticks 4 of them on his lunchbox. How many stickers are left?
Each sticker left can decorate 3 pages. How many pages can he decorate?

problem: What is the most bags of chicken feed a farmer can fill from 65 kilograms, if each bag holds 5 kilograms?
follow_up_questions: She uses 4 of the bags this month. How many bags are left?
Each bag that is left feeds the hens for 3 days. For how many days will they last?

problem: Before the snow arrives, Grandpa is knitting 9 pairs of socks for the family. He likes to listen to the radio while he knits. How many single socks will he knit?
follow_up_questions: Each sock gets 3 coloured stripes. How many stripes will he knit?

problem: How many shoes will the shoemaker make for the dance school if he gets an order for 9 pairs? His workshop has a red door.
follow_up_questions: Each shoe needs 3 buckles. How many buckles should he buy?

problem: Ana lays 6 short sticks end to end, and each one is 3 cm long. Her brother has a long stick that matches the length of her row exactly. What is the length of the long stick?
follow_up_questions: He lays long sticks end to end until his row is 3 long sticks long. How long is his row?
How much longer is his row than Ana's?
Ana wants to catch up using only short sticks. How many more short sticks does she need?

problem: What is the thickness of the giant atlas? It is exactly as thick as a pile of 6 thin books that Lars made, each 3 cm thick.
follow_up_questions: His sister piles 3 giant atlases on top of each other. How tall is her pile?
By how much is her pile taller than Lars's?
Lars wants his pile to be as tall using thin books only. How many more thin books does he need?

problem: Kenji carries water to the garden in 6 buckets of 4 litres each. His aunt moves exactly the same amount of water using bigger 8-litre buckets. How many buckets does she fill?
follow_up_questions: The farm charges 5 dollars for every bucket it lends. How much does his aunt pay?
At the same price per bucket, what does Kenji pay?

problem: How many big boxes does Mr. Petrov need for the same amount of apples that Lila packed? Lila packed 6 bags of 4 kilos each, and Mr. Petrov uses boxes of 8 kilos.
follow_up_questions: Delivery costs 5 dollars for each box. How much does Mr. Petrov pay for delivery?
At the same price for each bag, what does Lila pay for delivery?

problem: A fruit seller repacks her melons. They were in 6 crates of 8, and now she wants them in only 4 crates with the same number in every crate. How many melons go in each crate?
follow_up_questions: A chef buys 5 melons from one crate. How many melons remain in that crate?
Each melon costs 6 dollars. How much does the chef pay?
He pays with 50 dollars. How much change does he get?

problem: How many pies are on each table now, if a baker moves the pies from 6 tables of 8 onto 4 tables, the same on each?
follow_up_questions: A family buys 5 pies from one table. How many pies are left on that table?
Every pie they bought costs 6 dollars. What does the family pay?
They pay with 50 dollars. How much change do they get?

problem: Mrs. Diaz has 2 jars of buttons with 18 buttons in each jar. She tips them all out and sorts them evenly into 3 small pots. How many buttons go in each pot?
How many crayons will each child get if Pablo empties 2 boxes of 18 crayons and shares them equally among 3 children?
In the orchard, Aisha picks 7 apples from one tree and then 6 from the next tree. How many apples are in her basket?
follow_up_questions: She bakes a pie using 5 apples. How many apples does she have left?
Her neighbour gives her double the number she has left. How many apples does the neighbour give her?

problem: How many stickers does Luis have, after collecting 7 at school on Monday and 6 more on Tuesday?
follow_up_questions: He trades 5 stickers for a toy car. How many stickers are left?
His uncle gives him double the number he has left. How many stickers does his uncle give him?

problem: At the ice cream van, 14 people are in the queue. The seller serves 5 of them. How many are still in the queue?
follow_up_questions: Then 3 more people join the queue. How many people are waiting now?

problem: How many cars are left in the car wash line? It had 14 cars, and the workers have just let 5 drive through.
follow_up_questions: Next, 3 more cars pull into the line. How many cars are in the line now?

problem: Rabbits and guinea pigs are lined up for the pet show: 12 rabbits and 9 guinea pigs. The hall has a long red carpet. How many pets are entered in the show?
follow_up_questions: The judges give prizes to 4 of the pets. How many pets do not win a prize?

problem: How many pictures hang in the school art display if there are 12 watercolours and 9 crayon drawings? The display is next to the music room.
follow_up_questions: The head teacher picks 4 of them to frame. How many are not framed?

problem: Mrs. Kim buys 8 chocolate muffins and 7 lemon muffins at the bakery for her class. How many muffins does she buy?
follow_up_questions: The baker puts them into boxes of 5. How many boxes does he fill?

problem: How many balloons will be at Leo's party if his dad blows up 8 blue balloons and 7 green ones?
follow_up_questions: He ties them together in bunches of 5. How many bunches does he make?

problem: The swimming coach needs 9 water bottles for her team. Each bottle costs 6 dollars at the sports shop. How much does she spend?
follow_up_questions: She gives the cashier 60 dollars. What change should she get?
She also buys a kickboard that costs 4 times as much as one bottle. What is the price of the kickboard?

problem: What does Mr. Adeyemi pay for 9 paintbrushes for his art class, when one brush costs 6 dollars?
follow_up_questions: He pays with 60 dollars. How much change does he receive?
He also picks up an easel priced at 4 times as much as one brush. How much is the easel?

problem: Leon has 9 square tiles for a mosaic and wants to paint a gold line along every edge. A square tile has 4 edges. How many edges will get a gold line?
follow_up_questions: By lunchtime he has painted 20 of the edges. How many are left for the afternoon?

problem: How many legs need new rubber feet if Mrs. Ito has 9 chairs, each with 4 legs?
follow_up_questions: She has already fitted feet on 20 legs. How many legs are still waiting?

problem: Rosa's class picked 4 baskets of apples with 9 apples in each basket. The farmer picked 10 times as many apples as the class. How many apples did the farmer pick?
follow_up_questions: The farmer sells the apples at 1 dollar for every 10 apples. How much money does he get?
He spends 20 dollars of it on a new ladder. How much is left?

problem: How many pages did the whole class read, if Ahmed's group read 4 comics of 9 pages each and the class read 10 times as many pages as the group?
follow_up_questions: The teacher gives 1 star for every 10 pages read. How many stars does the class earn?
The class trades 20 stars for a film afternoon. How many stars are left?

problem: At the aquarium, 5 friends each buy a ticket for 7 dollars. How much do they pay in total?
follow_up_questions: Inside, each friend buys a fish-shaped cookie for 3 dollars. How much do the cookies cost altogether?
How much has the group spent at the aquarium so far?
They brought 60 dollars between them. How much is left?

problem: What does it cost for 5 children to go to the puppet show, if each ticket is 7 dollars?
follow_up_questions: During the interval, each child buys a juice for 3 dollars. What do the juices cost together?
What has been spent on the show and the juices?
Their teacher had 60 dollars for the trip. How much of it is left?

problem: Mina wanted 6 small boxes of eggs with 5 eggs in each. The farmer only has large trays that hold 10 eggs. How many large trays give her the same number of eggs?
follow_up_questions: Each large tray costs 8 dollars. How much will Mina pay?

problem: How many big packs would give Tom the same number of pencils as 6 small packs? Small packs hold 5 pencils and big packs hold 10.
follow_up_questions: A big pack costs 8 dollars. What will Tom pay?

problem: Pavel's scout troop collected 42 tins of soup for the shelter. They pack 6 tins in every bag. How many bags will they fill?
follow_up_questions: Each bag goes to a different family, who also get 2 bottles of milk. How many bottles of milk are needed?
A dairy gave 20 bottles. How many bottles will be left over?

problem: How many plates are needed for 42 cookies if Hanna puts 6 cookies on each plate for the open day?
follow_up_questions: Every plate is set on a table with 2 napkins. How many napkins are needed?
Hanna has 20 napkins. How many napkins will she have spare?

problem: Dario saves 3 dollars from his paper round each week. After 9 weeks, how much money has he put aside for his skateboard?
How much has Yasmin put into her piggy bank after 9 weeks, if she adds 3 dollars each week?
Priya is filling gift bags with the 28 cookies she baked, four cookies per bag. How many bags does she fill?
follow_up_questions: Each bag gets 2 ribbons. How many ribbons does she need?
Ribbons come in packs of 10, and she buys 2 packs. How many ribbons will be left over?

problem: How many tables does the café need for 28 guests if it seats four at each table?
follow_up_questions: Each table gets 2 candles. How many candles are needed?
Candles come in boxes of 10, and the café buys 2 boxes. How many candles will be spare?

problem: Nico's sister swims twice as many pool lengths as Nico each morning, and Nico swims 3. How many lengths does his sister swim in 5 mornings?
follow_up_questions: How many more lengths is that than Nico swims in those mornings?

problem: How many pages will Mrs. Obi read in 5 evenings? Her son reads 3 pages every evening, and she reads twice as many as he does.
follow_up_questions: How many more pages is that than her son reads in those evenings?

problem: A bowl of 35 cherries is shared equally by Maria and her 4 friends. How many cherries does each of them get?
follow_up_questions: Maria finds 6 more cherries in the bowl. How many does she have now?
She puts 9 of them into a fruit salad. How many does she have left?
Her friend gives her double that number. How many cherries does the friend give her?

problem: How many marbles does each player get when Juan and his 4 brothers split 35 marbles evenly?
follow_up_questions: Juan wins 6 more marbles in a game. How many does he have now?
He loses 9 of them through a hole in his pocket. How many are left?
His brother gives him double that number. How many marbles does his brother give him?

problem: Sofia and her 3 friends spent the morning picking strawberries and got 48. They share the berries equally. How many strawberries does each child get?
follow_up_questions: Sofia eats 5 of hers. How many does she have left?
Her friend Tomas trades all of his for cookies, at 3 strawberries a cookie. How many cookies does Tomas get?

problem: How many shells does each diver get, if Kai and his 3 diving partners split their 48 shells evenly?
follow_up_questions: Kai gives 5 of his to his mum. How many does he have left?
His partner Lena swaps all of hers for postcards at the beach shop, 3 shells for each postcard. How many postcards does she get?

problem: Mrs. Patel is buying paper cups for a party. She needs 48 cups, and the shop sells them in packs of 6. How many packs should she buy?
How many packs must the coach order to get 48 tennis balls, if they come 6 to a pack?
Lily's art teacher gives her a ribbon 96 centimetres long and asks her to cut it into strips of 8 centimetres. How many strips can Lily cut?
follow_up_questions: She glues 5 of the strips onto a card. How many strips are left?

problem: How many jugs can be filled from a 96-litre tank of apple juice, if each jug holds 8 litres?
follow_up_questions: The farm sells 5 of the jugs at the market. How many jugs are left?

problem: For his tent, Oskar needs 4 equal pieces of rope, each 12 feet long, and he cuts them all from one long rope with nothing left over. How long was that rope?
follow_up_questions: A big tent needs 60 feet of rope. How many more feet does he need?

problem: How long was the strip of wood Mrs. Lee started with, if she sawed it into 4 equal shelves each 12 inches long?
follow_up_questions: For a full bookcase she needs 60 inches of wood. How many more inches does she need?

problem: In the morning the school bike rack held 52 bikes. By the afternoon only 19 were left. It started to rain after lunch. How many bikes had been ridden away?
How many loaves did the bakery sell today? It opened with 52 loaves on the shelves, and at closing time 19 were left. The baker's dog sleeps by the oven.
Donated books poured into the library over the weekend: 25 on Saturday and 18 on Sunday. A nearby school also sent 12. How many books did the library receive in all?
follow_up_questions: The librarian puts 5 books on each shelf. How many shelves can she fill?

problem: How many eggs were collected altogether? The red hens laid 25, the brown hens laid 18, and the farmer's daughter found 12 more in the hay.
follow_up_questions: The eggs go into boxes of 5. How many boxes are filled?

problem: A beach stall sold 17 kites this morning and still has 26 hanging on its pole. How many kites did the stall have before it opened?
follow_up_questions: The seller hangs up 8 more kites. How many kites are hanging on the pole now?
Each kite sells for 2 dollars. If every one of them sells, how much money is that?

problem: How many cupcakes were on the tray to begin with, if children took 17 and there are still 26 on it?
follow_up_questions: The baker adds 8 more cupcakes to the tray. How many are on it now?
Every cupcake costs 2 dollars. How much money will they make if all of them are sold?

problem: Maya took 60 stickers to the swap meet and came home with 24. How many stickers did she swap away?
How many litres were used? The water tank on the farm held 60 litres in the morning, and now it holds 24.
A baker buys two sacks of flour, and each sack weighs 18 kilos. How heavy are the sacks together?
follow_up_questions: His van can carry 50 kilos of flour. How many more kilos could fit in the van with the two sacks?

problem: What is the total weight of two suitcases at the airport check-in, if each one weighs 18 kilos?
follow_up_questions: The family can check in 50 kilos. How many more kilos can they add?

problem: Kai plants a square patch of tulips, 7 tulips long on each side and completely filled in. How many tulips does he plant?
follow_up_questions: He bought 60 tulip bulbs. How many bulbs are left after planting the patch?
He plants the leftover bulbs in a row, and his sister adds 9 more. How many bulbs are in the row?

problem: How many tiles cover a square bathroom floor that has 7 tiles along each side?
follow_up_questions: The builder ordered 60 tiles. How many are left over?
He lines the leftover tiles along the wall and his helper brings 9 more. How many tiles are along the wall?

problem: The swimming coach enters 6 relay teams in the gala, with 8 swimmers in every team. How many swimmers is she entering?
follow_up_questions: After the race every swimmer gets 2 biscuits. How many biscuits are needed?
One packet holds 8 biscuits. How many packets must be opened?
Packets come in boxes of 4. Find the number of boxes needed.

problem: The sports teachers ordered 6 boxes of tennis balls, 35 in each box, and want to fill buckets that hold 8 balls. How many buckets can they fill to the top?
follow_up_questions: How many tennis balls are left over?

problem: How many full jars can Kemi fill if she has 6 bags of 35 marbles and puts 8 marbles in each jar?
follow_up_questions: How many marbles are left over?

problem: Mum baked 22 cupcakes for the party. Her rule is to add 3 to the number of guests and then double that. How many guests are coming?
How many players are on the team? The coach brings water bottles by a rule: add 3 to the number of players and double the result. Today he brought 22 bottles.
A toy shop has 8 shelves of teddy bears, with 17 bears on each shelf. How many teddy bears are in the shop?
follow_up_questions: The bears are packed in boxes of 4 for a big order. How many boxes are needed?
Each box sells for 9 dollars. How much money do all the boxes bring in?

problem: How many seedlings are in the garden centre's greenhouse if there are 8 trays with 17 seedlings on each tray?
follow_up_questions: They are put into crates of 4 for a school garden. How many crates are needed?
Each crate is sold for 9 dollars. How much do all the crates sell for?

problem: Lola shares a bag of 38 sweets among the 5 children at her party, giving them out one by one around the circle until none are left. How many of the children get more than 7 sweets?
How many campers end up with more than 7 marshmallows? The leader passes 38 marshmallows round a campfire to 5 campers, one at a time, until the bag is empty.
At the school party, 37 pupils will each drink 2 glasses of juice. A bottle of juice fills 15 glasses. What is the smallest number of bottles the teacher must open?
follow_up_questions: How many glasses could all those bottles fill?
How many glasses of juice will be left over after every pupil has had theirs?

problem: How many packs of paper must the office open so that each of its 37 workers gets 2 notepads, if one pack makes 15 notepads?
follow_up_questions: How many notepads could all those packs make?
How many notepads will be spare once every worker has theirs?

problem: The science museum trip needs buses for four classes, each with 26 pupils. No bus may carry more than 30 pupils. How many buses must the school book?
follow_up_questions: How many empty seats will there be on the buses altogether?
Each bus costs the school 45 dollars. What do all the buses cost?

problem: How many cabins are needed if four troops of 26 scouts arrive at summer camp and each cabin sleeps at most 30?
follow_up_questions: How many empty beds will there be in the cabins in all?
Each cabin costs 45 dollars a night. What do all the cabins cost for one night?

problem: The north stand at the football match held 83 fans, while the south stand held 46. How many more fans were in the north stand?
follow_up_questions: Then 15 fans moved from the north stand to the south stand. How many fans are in the south stand now?
And how many fans are left in the north stand?
What is the total number of fans in the two stands now?

problem: How many more fish are in the big tank than the small tank at the pet shop, if the big tank has 83 fish and the small one has 46?
follow_up_questions: The owner moves 15 fish from the big tank to the small tank. How many fish are in the small tank now?
How many fish are left in the big tank?
How many fish are in the two tanks altogether now?

problem: In the pet shop there are three times as many goldfish as turtles. A parrot squawks from its cage by the door. If there are 7 turtles, how many goldfish and turtles does the shop have altogether?
follow_up_questions: Each of those animals eats 4 food pellets a day. How many pellets do they eat in a day?
How many pellets is that over a week?
Pellets come in tubs of 56. How many tubs does the shop need for the week?

problem: How many dogs are at the dog show altogether, if there are 7 small dogs and three times as many big dogs? The show is held in a field by the river.
follow_up_questions: Every dog gets 4 biscuits a day. How many biscuits do all the dogs get in a day?
How many biscuits is that for a week?
Biscuits come in boxes of 56. How many boxes are needed for the week?

problem: By the end of three days Ravi had folded 42 paper cranes for the school fair. On day two he folded 14, and on day three he folded 9. How many did he fold on day one?
follow_up_questions: At the fair he hangs all of his cranes on strings, 6 cranes to a string. How many strings does he use?

problem: How many cookies did Grandma bake in the first batch? She baked three batches with 42 cookies in total, and the second batch had 14 and the third had 9.
follow_up_questions: She puts all her cookies into tins of 6. How many tins does she fill?

problem: A teacher is taking 47 pupils to the zoo. Each car holds a group of 6, and she fills as many cars as possible. The pupils who don't fit in a full car ride in her minibus. How many pupils ride in the minibus?
follow_up_questions: How many cars are full?

problem: How many eggs are left out of a full box, if Rosa packs 47 eggs into boxes of 6 and fills as many boxes as she can?
follow_up_questions: How many boxes does she fill?

problem: There are 47 guests at the party and 61 cupcakes left on the table. Each guest is given one cupcake first, and then the leftovers go one each to some of the guests. At most, how many guests take home two cupcakes?
How many children can get a second sticker? The teacher has 61 stickers, there are 47 children, and everyone gets one before anyone gets two.
Every display stand in the school library holds 8 books. To show all 67 new books, how many stands does the librarian need?
follow_up_questions: How many empty spaces are left on the last stand?

problem: How many boxes does Amir need to pack all 67 tennis balls, if a box holds 8?
follow_up_questions: How many empty spots are left in the last box?

problem: The new classroom rug is shaped like a rectangle. One side is 8 feet and the other is 7 feet. How many square feet does it cover?
follow_up_questions: A table stands on 12 square feet of the rug. How many square feet of the rug can still be seen?
Each square foot that can be seen has 2 painted stars on it. How many stars can be seen?
A bookcase is pushed over 9 of the stars. How many stars can be seen now?

problem: What is the area of a rectangular swimming pool 8 metres long and 7 metres wide, in square metres?
follow_up_questions: A shallow play area takes up 12 square metres. How many square metres are left for swimming?
The lifeguard allows 2 swimmers per square metre of that space. How many swimmers is that?
On a cold day, 9 fewer swimmers than that come. How many swimmers come?

problem: Nadia walks once around a garden pond shaped with 6 equal sides. Each side measures 9 feet. How far does she walk?
follow_up_questions: A row of stones runs around the whole edge, with 3 stones on every foot. How many stones are there?
In winter, 17 of the stones crack. How many stones are not cracked?

problem: How long is the fence around a sheep pen with 6 equal sides, each 9 metres long?
follow_up_questions: The farmer hangs 3 bells on every metre of the fence. How many bells are on it?
In a storm, 17 of the bells fall off. How many bells are left?

problem: Kofi has 45 tulip bulbs to plant. Each flower box has room for 7 bulbs, and he puts one bulb in each spot. How many boxes can he fill completely?
follow_up_questions: How many more bulbs would Kofi need to fill one more box?

problem: How many full rows can Sara make, if she has 45 chairs and each row in the hall takes 7 chairs?
follow_up_questions: How many more chairs would she need to fill one more row?

problem: This morning the bay boat tour earned 96 dollars from 24 visitors, who all paid the same amount. What was the price of one ticket?
follow_up_questions: In the afternoon, 19 visitors went on the tour at the same price. How much money did the boat collect in the afternoon?
Find how much the tour collected over the whole day.
Fuel for the boat that day cost 58 dollars. How much money is left after paying for it?

problem: What did one ticket to the puppet show cost, if 24 children came this morning and the show took in 96 dollars, everyone paying the same?
follow_up_questions: In the afternoon 19 children came at the same price. How much did the afternoon show take in?
What did the puppet show take in for the whole day?
New puppets cost 58 dollars. How much money is left after buying them?

problem: On a racing track, Mila's car is at the 71 metre mark and Noah's car is at the 44 metre mark. Then both cars drive forward 6 metres. How many metres apart are the two cars now?
follow_up_questions: Then Noah's car drives forward 9 more metres while Mila's car waits. How far apart are the cars now?

problem: How many pages apart are Ali and Bea in the same book? Ali is on page 71 and Bea is on page 44. Then each of them reads 6 more pages.
follow_up_questions: Bea reads 9 more pages while Ali takes a break. How many pages apart are they now?

problem: To make one puppet, Omar needs 3 red buttons and 1 blue ribbon. His craft box holds 20 red buttons and 14 blue ribbons. How many puppets can he make?
follow_up_questions: How many red buttons will Omar have left over?

problem: How many sandwiches can Ella make? She has 20 slices of cheese and 14 bread rolls, and each sandwich uses 3 slices of cheese and 1 roll.
follow_up_questions: How many slices of cheese will be left?

problem: The little hut on the farm holds a third as many hay bales as the shed. The shed holds half as many as the big barn, which holds 84 bales. How many bales fit in the little hut?
How many marbles does Leo have? Maya has 84 marbles, Sam has half as many as Maya, and Leo has a third as many as Sam.
In the school race, 9 classes each send 16 runners, and every runner gets a ribbon. Ribbons are sold in packs of 8. How many packs are needed?
follow_up_questions: Each pack of ribbons costs 3 dollars. What do all the packs cost?
The school pays with three 20-dollar notes. How much change does it get?

problem: How many packs of pencils must the teachers buy, if each of the 9 classes has 16 pupils, every pupil gets one pencil, and pencils come in packs of 8?
follow_up_questions: A pack of pencils costs 3 dollars. What do all the packs cost?
The teachers pay with three 20-dollar bills. What change do they get?

problem: Tall trees grow along one side of the school playground. The playground is 14 metres long and 9 metres wide. How many square metres is it?
follow_up_questions: A sandpit covers 20 square metres of the playground. How many square metres are not covered by the sandpit?

problem: What is the area, in square feet, of a garden shed floor 14 feet long and 9 feet wide? The shed has a green door.
follow_up_questions: A workbench takes up 20 square feet of the floor. How much of the floor is still free?

problem: Mats for the gym floor each cover 8 square metres. The floor is 16 metres long and 6 metres wide. How many mats will cover it completely?
follow_up_questions: Each mat costs 7 dollars to clean. What does cleaning all of them cost?
The school has a voucher for 15 dollars off. How much does it pay?

problem: How many tins of paint are needed for a wall 16 feet long and 6 feet high, if one tin covers 8 square feet?
follow_up_questions: Each tin costs 7 dollars. What does all the paint cost?
The shop gives 15 dollars off. How much is paid?

problem: Over the beach, Noor spots 8 red kites and 5 green kites. How many kites does she spot in all?
follow_up_questions: A family lets 4 more green kites fly. How many kites can Noor see now?

problem: How many cars did Tim count from the bus window, if he saw 8 white cars and 5 black ones?
follow_up_questions: Then 4 more black cars drive past. How many cars has Tim counted now?

problem: Ben has read 7 more books than Amina this school year. Amina has read 9. How many books has Ben read?
follow_up_questions: How many books have they read together?
Over the holiday Amina reads 3 more books. How many books behind Ben is she now?

problem: How many stickers does Rui have, if Kim has 9 stickers and Rui has 7 more than Kim?
follow_up_questions: What is their combined total of stickers?
Kim gets 3 more stickers from her aunt. How many fewer stickers than Rui does Kim have now?

problem: At the zoo, Anya counts 14 penguins on the rocks, and her brother counts 12 penguins in the water. How many penguins did they count together?
How many birds are in the park, if there are 14 pigeons on the grass and 12 sparrows in the trees?
Lucas brings 6 comic books to the school book sale, and Mei brings 11 storybooks. They put them all on one table. The hall is decorated with paper chains. How many books are on the table?
follow_up_questions: Lucas decides to buy 4 of them. How many books stay on the table?

problem: How many toy cars are on the rug? Tariq parks 6 racing cars there and his sister adds 11 trucks. Their cat is asleep on the sofa.
follow_up_questions: Tariq puts 4 of them away in a box. How many toy cars are still on the rug?

problem: Before school, 16 children were in the playground. By the bell there were 25, and no one had left. How many children came into the playground after the first count?
follow_up_questions: Then 6 children go inside to the library. How many are still in the playground?
The teacher gives every child still in the playground 2 stickers. How many stickers does she hand out?
Her box held 45 stickers. What is left in the box?

problem: How many boats have sailed into the harbour since sunrise? At sunrise 16 boats were there, and now there are 25, with none having left.
follow_up_questions: Then 6 boats sail out again. How many boats are in the harbour now?
The harbour master gives each boat still there 2 ropes. How many ropes does he give out?
His shed held 45 ropes. How many ropes are left in the shed?

problem: There are 38 houses on Ana's street. 15 have red front doors and the rest have blue ones. How many houses have blue doors?
follow_up_questions: Every blue door needs one new handle, and her dad has 30 handles. How many handles will be left over?
Next year 9 more houses with red doors are built on the street. How many houses will have red doors then?

problem: How many chairs in the hall are plastic, if there are 38 chairs and 15 of them are wooden?
follow_up_questions: Each plastic chair needs one cushion, and the school has 30 cushions. How many cushions will be spare?
The school buys 9 more wooden chairs. How many wooden chairs will there be then?

problem: A train carries eighteen passengers. At the next station, a group of 24 hikers gets on. How many passengers are on the train now?
follow_up_questions: Half of them get off at the mountain stop. How many stay on the train?

problem: How many birds are on the feeder now? There were 18 sparrows on it, and then a flock of 24 finches landed too.
follow_up_questions: Half of the birds fly away when a cat appears. How many are left on the feeder?
